tasks.short: Inspect and measure the hot section part, look up its repair limits in the engine manual, compare the measurements, decide serviceable, repairable or scrap, and record the finding on the job card.

steps.what: Aircraft mechanic inspects the engine hot section part and measures wear, cracks and burns
Aircraft mechanic looks up the repair limits in the engine manual for the part number and revision
Aircraft mechanic compares the measurements with the limits
Aircraft mechanic determines repair limits for engine hot section parts: serviceable, repairable or scrap
Aircraft mechanic writes the findings and decision on the paper job card and signs it

tasks.design: The electronic job card in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) opens the engine manual section for the part number, engine serial and current revision, with the limits as fields. Measurements entered on the card are compared with those limits in code and out-of-limit values are flagged. The mechanic decides and signs the card electronically. Release to service stays with authorised certifying staff, and going paperless needs the aviation authority's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Limits were looked up in the manual by hand and compared on paper job cards.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems run electronic job cards with e-signature and links to manual revisions.
tasks.still_hard: Damage that falls between manual limits needs an engineering decision.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a crack's shape that the limit table does not describe.

reach.learn: Whether flagged comparisons speed up release checks.

evidence.claim: AMOS e-jobcards are created and completed in the system and signed through a PDF overlay; SunExpress went live in 2023 as an approved paperless operator.
In a two-month parallel run, the paper technical log had 52 errors and the electronic log had 1.
Part-145 requires detailed maintenance records kept for 3 years, protected from alteration, and going paperless needs the authority's approval.

assumptions: Boundary: from the removed part to the signed job card; repair and release to service are outside.
Input contract: engine manual revisions from the manufacturer loaded by technical records; part data from the engine record; fallback is the paper manual and job card.
Inspecting and deciding do not change.
The authority approves the electronic records before use.
s5 is part of keeping repair logs, which sibling task 49-3011.00:9948 covers; its saving is counted there, so s5 keeps its full time here.
Writing and signing the job card is the mechanic's own record in the maintenance system, an ordinary save, so it needs no separate approval.

incremental.description: Aircraft mechanic reports limit fields that do not match the manual.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: limits are loaded for only about half of the engine types serviced, so the rest are looked up and compared by hand (8.2); high: limits loaded for all engine types (17.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The aircraft mechanic keeps inspecting and deciding on parts; manual look-ups and paper job cards shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A mechanic whose records are right the first time.
